title: Jail exposure can remain heavy and unequal while the aggregate jail population declines
source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics Census of Jails and Jail Inmates in 2024 statistical tables
geography: United States local jails; midyear 2024 custody and July 2023-June 2024 admissions, with comparison to 2014

observations.period: Midyear 2024 custody; admissions July 2023-June 2024; decade comparison to 2014

denominator.unit: local-jail custody and admission events; exact unique-person denominator is not available from the summary

midyear_custody.unit: people held in local jails at midyear 2024

admissions.unit: local-jail admissions from July 2023 through June 2024

unconvicted_share.unit: percent of people held at midyear who had not been convicted

average_stay_before_release.unit: average days people admitted spent in jail before release

racial_rate_difference.value: 566 Black residents per 100,000 compared with 149 white residents per 100,000

decade_change.value: midyear jail population 12% lower and annual admissions 31% lower than 2014

observations.method: BJS statistical tables from the Census of Jails covering custody, admissions, conviction status, length of stay, demographics, capacity, staffing, and community supervision measures.
observations.uncertainty: Admissions are events and can include repeat admissions; custody is not a unique-person life history. The summary does not link arrest, pretrial decision, case disposition, release conditions, housing, work, health, supervision, or later justice contact.
observations.subgroup: People held in local jails, with race-specific incarceration-rate comparisons and unconvicted status; local variation and individual case pathways are not followed in the summary.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower population and admissions can reflect reduced detention, changed policing or court practice, population change, or other administrative shifts. A high unconvicted share does not establish innocence or wrongful detention, and a racial rate gap does not identify its causes.

related_sources.claim: BJS methodology and Census of Jails data-collection context.
Related BJS correctional-population context for community supervision and correctional trends.

boundary: This record measures local-jail custody, admissions, conviction status, stay length, racial rate differences, and decade change. It does not establish crime causation, wrongful detention, individual case outcomes, reentry success, public safety, or trust.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official BJS 2024 jail statistical tables and methodology pages reviewed; underlying jail-level microdata are not retained
